paragraphs: Friend, here's the thing that jumps out at me. God's word came true, every piece of it. Jeremiah had told Zedekiah that surrendering meant living and running meant being caught (Jeremiah 38:17-18), and Zedekiah ran at night anyway. When God says something is coming, it comes, and that includes His warnings.

But look who else God's word reached. Ebed-melech, the Cushite who got Jeremiah pulled out of that cistern, was the one the LORD sent a message to while Jeremiah was still confined in the courtyard of the guard: "For I will surely rescue you so that you do not fall by the sword." (Jeremiah 39:18) The reason is right there in the verse: "Because you have trusted in Me…" The city fell, but God's promise to the man who trusted Him was rescue.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Trusting God is not about how loud you are or how high you sit, because Ebed-melech was a court official and the king still ran. Trust what God says, because He keeps His word when it warns and when it saves. And hear me on this one: this story isn't over, so keep your oven on.
